text:
Rafael Mendes: We need to update the on-call runbook + do a quick training pass before we enable one-click rollback for Optimize configs in prod. The last incident was way too manual.

Rafael Mendes: I drafted a checklist for “rollback success validation” + comms templates. Want SRE + Obs sign-off. @Kira Thompson can you fold into the runbook page? @Tomáš Novák can you sanity-check incident process bits?

Kira Thompson: Yep. Drop the checklist here and I’ll port it into Confluence under eng-sre/runbooks. Also: do we want separate sections for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?

Rafael Mendes: For v1 I’d keep one main flow with “deployment mode notes” callouts. Biggest diff is who gets paged + where to check propagation status.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Also please include explicit MTTR target and “stop the bleeding” language. If rollback isn’t restoring SLOs within 10 min, escalate.

Neha Kapoor: Agree. We also need a drill plan. We can’t just ship this and hope folks read the doc.

Rafael Mendes: Here’s the proposed validation checklist (post-rollback):

Rafael Mendes: 1) Confirm rollback request succeeded
- Console: Rollback status shows “Completed” (not just “Submitted”)
- API: `rollback_status=COMPLETED` with `correlation_id`
- Audit log entry exists: `optimize.config.rollback_rolled_back` (and not only `rollback_attempted`)

Rafael Mendes: 2) Confirm runtime propagation converged
- Dashboard: “Config Apply / Rollback Propagation” panel -> all shards/replicas >= 99% applied for the scope (route/model/customer/region)
- If < 99% after 3 min: check for “lease stuck” / “apply lock held” and page Runtime oncall

Rafael Mendes: 3) Confirm impact metrics are trending back
- p95 latency for affected route/model (5m window) back within +10% of baseline OR error budget gate OK
- error rate (5xx + model errors) not elevated
- saturation indicators: GPU util, queue depth, scheduler backpressure not worse than pre-change

Rafael Mendes: 4) Confirm no new regressions
- Check “Config Change Health” dashboard for any spike in `config_apply_failure_total` or `stuck_rollout_total`
- Confirm no flood of `kv_cache_invalidate_errors` (runtime metric)

Rafael Mendes: 5) Confirm customer-facing symptoms are resolved
- If incident: confirm user-reported endpoints stabilize; watch support ticket volume / #support-escalations for 10-15 min

Rafael Mendes: 6) Close the loop
- Update incident channel with correlation_id + rolled back version
- Add link to audit log entry + Console history diff

Allison Grant: Looks good. Two things:
1) specify exact dashboards / queries (people will miss the right panels).
2) add “what to screenshot/save” for postmortem (audit event + diff view + metrics panels).

Aisha Bello: +1. We should put the exact metric names and default thresholds in the runbook so someone can do it half-asleep.

Tomáš Novák: Process-wise: add a small decision tree. If it’s clearly config-related regression, rollback is the primary mitigation. If unclear, do canary rollback? Or rollback scoped (if we support scoping by route/model only).

Rafael Mendes: For v1 rollback is per scope (route/model/customer deployment scope), but it’s still whole-config for that scope. We should encourage smallest blast radius first when possible.

Sean Gallagher: Add escalation triggers:
- rollback attempt fails OR status stuck > 5 min
- propagation < 95% after 5 min
- latency doesn’t improve within 10 min
- repeated rollbacks > 2 in 30 min (something deeper is wrong)

Kira Thompson: Can you also include comms templates? Especially for #incidents and for CS/customer comms.

Rafael Mendes: Comms templates draft:

Rafael Mendes: (A) #incidents update template
“Mitigation: Executed Optimize config rollback for scope=<SCOPE> from version <BAD_VER> -> <GOOD_VER>.
- Trigger: <latency/error spike> after config change
- Correlation ID: <CID>
- Status: <Submitted/In progress/Completed>
- Propagation: <xx%> replicas applied
- Metrics: p95=<value> (baseline <value>), err_rate=<value>
Next update in <5/10> min.”

Rafael Mendes: (B) Customer-facing status template (for CS to adapt)
“We identified an issue related to a recent performance optimization configuration change affecting <region/service>. We have reverted that configuration and are monitoring recovery. Current status: <recovering/mitigated>. Next update in <time>.”

Rafael Mendes: (C) Post-mitigation confirmation
“Rollback completed and propagation converged. Metrics have returned to normal ranges. Continuing to monitor for 15 min. We’ll follow up with a detailed RCA.”

Tomáš Novák: Nice. Add: if we’re in an official SEV, ensure comms go through incident commander. Not every oncaller should ping customers directly.

Kira Thompson: I’ll add a “Comms ownership” note: SRE updates incident channel; Support/CS handles customer updates; IC approves external message.

Devon Price: (incident-bot) FYI: once the rollback feature lands, incident-bot can auto-post rollback deep links if we include the correlation_id in the incident channel topic. We should document that too.

Allison Grant: Please include the “correlation_id” discipline in the runbook. It’s the only way we tie audit logs -> rollout status -> metrics.

Aisha Bello: Can we standardize a quick query snippet?
- `cid=<CID>` filter in logs/traces
- dashboard link parameters
If we have those, on-call can paste in and go.

Rafael Mendes: Good call. I’ll add a “copy/paste snippets” section.

Sean Gallagher: Training plan proposal:
- 30 min walkthrough in #eng-sre + record it
- 1 game-day in staging: deliberately apply a bad batching config, then rollback
- quiz in the on-call handoff doc: “where do you find applied version? how do you confirm propagation?”

Neha Kapoor: +1 on game-day. Also include runtime folks (Mateo/Sofia) so we validate edge cases (cache invalidation/warmup).

Kira Thompson: Logistics: I can schedule a 30-min training next Tue/Thu. Who’s presenting? Rafael + Allison?

Rafael Mendes: I can present flow + checklist. Allison covers dashboards. Devon can demo incident-bot messages if ready.

Devon Price: Works. I’ll prep a quick slide with “what incident-bot posts + how to use rollback deep link”.

Allison Grant: I’ll add exact dashboard names + links. Please confirm the canonical ones are:
- “Config Change Health”
- “Optimize Config Apply/Rollback Propagation”
- “Inference Latency by Route/Model (p50/p95/p99)” (with region filter)

Rafael Mendes: Yes + add error rate panel (5xx + model errors). Also a note: if this is Dedicated customer, use tenant-scoped dashboards.

incident-bot: (system) Reminder set by Rafael Mendes: “Draft runbook updates + training invite” in 2 hours.

Tomáš Novák: One more: include a “pitfalls” section:
- rollback succeeded but latency still bad because saturation persists
- partial improvement due to traffic shift / cache warmup
- repeated rollbacks toggling batching can thrash caches

Rafael Mendes: Adding. Also: “don’t keep clicking rollback” — use idempotency key / check status first.

Sean Gallagher: Great. Once Kira posts the Confluence link, I’ll sign off if it includes MTTR/escalation triggers.

Kira Thompson: Action items:
- Rafael: finalize checklist + pitfalls + copy/paste queries
- Allison/Aisha: dashboard links + thresholds
- Devon: incident-bot notes
- Kira: port into runbook + add Hosted/Dedicated/Private notes
- Sean/Neha: review + approve before we train

Rafael Mendes: Sounds good. I’ll send the final text in this thread today so Kira can paste. (reactions: :thumbsup: from Sean Gallagher, Neha Kapoor, Allison Grant)
